corpus.procedure: keyword search of the venues switched on in venues.yaml, through OpenAlex, then the works most cited among the hits and among what the paper cites, kept when they are in those venues

claims.text: Existing work explains learning and action once theories, vocabularies, or awareness advantages exist; this paper supplies the pre-Bayesian passage from represented-class failure to a question, a fallible new representation, formulation, and renewed Bayesian judgment. Its distinctive economic and epistemic results are that an agent can value a finer actionable distinction before representing its answers, and that evidence generating a truth-blind representation cannot be counted again as independent validation. Embedding that passage in strategic interaction provides a mechanism by which play exposes or conceals coarse languages and establishes the existence of absorbing configurations with heterogeneous terminal languages and payoffs. The contribution is therefore upstream: question histories and rational stopping points can generate strategic heterogeneity before priors over the resulting theories are available. The paper endogenizes the strategically consequential transition into a new hypothesis space while leaving the semantic act that produces it primitive.

nearest.establishes: A verbal theory of the origin of novel entrepreneurial beliefs and strategies that extend beyond prior experience, through theorizing triggered by experiential and observational fragments, imagination of possibilities, and reasoning and justification, aggregated socially through interaction and self-selection.
nearest.citation: Felin & Zenger (2009). Entrepreneurs as theorists: on the origins of collective beliefs and novel strategies
retrieved_by: cited by 8 of the retrieved works

nearest.establishes: Simulations in which cognition is a low-dimensional representation of a higher-dimensional landscape show that crude representations guide and constrain experiential search, and that shifting the representation is itself a mode of adaptation, offset by the loss of tacit knowledge tied to the prior cognition.
nearest.citation: Gavetti & Levinthal (2000). Looking Forward and Looking Backward: Cognitive and Experiential Search
retrieved_by: cited by 5 of the retrieved works

nearest.establishes: A choice-based model of a decision maker aware of her own unawareness, who anticipates discovering currently indescribable consequences, assigns a 'utility of the unknown' to them, and revises her sense of residual ignorance after discoveries, nesting reverse Bayesian updating as a special case.
nearest.citation: Karni & Vierø (2017). Awareness of unawareness: A theory of decision making in the face of ignorance
retrieved_by: cited by 5 of the retrieved works

nearest.establishes: A formal theory of subjective rationality and self-confirming equilibrium in which erroneous counterfactual beliefs go unrefuted by equilibrium play, so that a firm can sustain a performance advantage over subjectively rational competitors who persist in suboptimal strategies.
nearest.citation: Ryall (2003). Subjective Rationality, Self–Confirming Equilibrium, and Corporate Strategy
retrieved_by: cited by 4 of the retrieved works

nearest.establishes: An axiomatic choice-based model of growing awareness in which discovery of new acts, consequences or act-consequence links expands the state space and beliefs are extended by 'reverse Bayesian' proportional shifting of probability mass, the discovery itself being taken as given.
nearest.citation: Karni & Vierø (2013). “Reverse Bayesianism”: A Choice-Based Theory of Growing Awareness
retrieved_by: cited by 6 of the retrieved works

claims.rationale: Felin & Zenger (2009) (W2062762321), which the paper does not cite, poses the question in substance: where novel beliefs and theories come from when they extend beyond experience, the step before a theory is in hand; it answers verbally and states none of the claim's formal results (pricing a finer distinction before its answers are represented, no evidential reuse of the generating record, absorbing configurations with heterogeneous terminal languages). The awareness models (W2145868584, W2115460181) take the newly expanded space as given and model beliefs or attitudes around it, Gavetti & Levinthal (W2113812196) treats representation shifts without modeling how a failed one is replaced, and Ryall (2003) (W2152908192) gives persistent strategic differences within a fixed belief space, so none states the claim; hence a new answer to a question already posed. The call on poses_question for W2062762321 is the deciding one and is close: it does not frame the starting point as the failure of a causal language.

question.text: How an actor whose causal language has failed comes to possess a new one: the step before a theory, or at least a hypothesis space, exists.

coverage.statement: Venues searched: utd24, ft50, cabs4star, cabs4 (150 journals, 150 resolved in OpenAlex). 4 queries from the contribution claim and the title returned 25 hits; 20 works were added as the most cited among them (16 such works lay outside the venues and were dropped). Candidates shown to the model: 45, of which 5 have no abstract and were seen by title, venue and year only. 20 were also read from their introduction (14 from the journal's licensed copies, 6 from open-access copies); the rest have no copy the journal holds or could fetch. Not covered: work outside the venues searched, books, work without an abstract, beyond its title, non-English work, grey literature.
